wa_cascade_peak_east_ridge.primary: Up the Cascade-Johannesburg Couloir to the C-J col

why.Cascade Pass, Mixup Arm and the Cache Gl: Mid to late season, once the couloir snow breaks up and its rock and ice fall make it too risky; a longer walk and some glacier travel, but it never enters the chute.

wa_castle_peak_pasayten_scramble.primary: Ross Lake boat crossing, Lightning Creek trail and the abandoned Freezeout Creek trail

why.The crest trail north from Harts Pass to: When you would rather walk than arrange a boat crossing, and can spare the extra days on foot once the high road to Harts Pass has opened, usually in July.

wa_castle_peak_pasayten_the_drawbridge.primary: Ross Lake boat crossing, Lightning Creek and the abandoned Freezeout Creek trail to the north-face glacier

why.Pacific Crest Trail north from Harts Pas: When you have no boat or water taxi and will walk the roughly 27 miles of crest in, after the Harts Pass road opens, usually in July.

wa_cathedral_peak_last_rites.primary: Andrews Creek trail #504 from the Chewuch River road

why.Cathedral Driveway trail #510A from Loom: When you want the shortest walk and least climbing in, and can accept a drive about two hours longer and 1,300 ft of climbing on the way out.
why.Thirtymile Trailhead and the Chewuch Riv: When linking the climb with the Remmel Lake country; a longer walk than the Andrews Creek way, on gentler valley trail.

wa_cathedral_peak_pasayten_se_buttress.primary: Andrews Creek trail #504 from the Chewuch River road

why.Cathedral Driveway trail #510A from Loom: When you want the shortest walk and least climbing in, and can accept a drive about two hours longer and 1,300 ft of climbing on the way out.
why.Thirtymile Trailhead and the Chewuch Riv: When linking the climb with the Remmel Lake country; a longer walk than the Andrews Creek way, on gentler valley trail.

wa_cathedral_peak_southwest_route.primary: Andrews Creek trail #504 to Upper Cathedral Lake, then the trail toward Cathedral Pass

why.Cathedral Driveway trail #510A from Loom: When you want the shortest walk and least climbing in, and can accept a much longer drive from Loomis and a climb out at the end.
why.Thirtymile Trailhead and the Chewuch Riv: When linking the climb with the Remmel Lake country; a longer walk than the Andrews Creek way, on gentler valley trail.

wa_cathedral_rock_standard.primary: Cathedral Pass trail #1345 from the Cle Elum River road end

why.Peggy's Pond, gaining the summit gully f: When splitting the trip with a night at the last reliable water, or combining the climb with Mount Daniel; the final ledges into the pond are exposed.

why.Source Lake basin to the divide (summer: Summer and fall, once the snow is gone and the buttress is climbed as a rock route; the basin path avoids the early-season slide gully.

wa_chikamin_peak_southeast_slopes.primary: PCT from Snoqualmie Pass, leaving the trail half a mile short of Chikamin Pass

why.Mineral Creek and Park Lakes, then the g: When doing it as a day trip: about 15 miles round trip against roughly 24 from the pass, though the tread is brushy and rough low down.

wa_chiwawa_mountain_southwest.primary: Trinity and the Chiwawa River Trail to Chiwawa Basin and the 6,300 ft benches

why.Phelps Creek variant to the col west of: When you prefer the shorter line on paper from Phelps Creek and can handle a trail-less bushwhack with no good camp; for parties who know the area.

wa_clark_mountain_west_ridge.primary: Boulder Pass and the Walrus Glacier — the glacier line

why.Boulder Creek and the sheepherder's trai: Late in the season, or when you have no glacier gear, once the crevasses on the glacier have opened up; a walk-up line from the same basin.

why.Buck Creek Trail from Trinity, over Buck: When starting from the Trinity side and making a longer multi-day trip of it, instead of the shorter Phelps Creek day over Spider Gap.
why.Railroad Creek from Holden Village: When you are already based at Holden Village, reached by the Lake Chelan boat and a shuttle; the longest way in with the most fixed logistics.
